## Data

This data is from the Federal Reserve Economic Data database (FRED). This is an online database consisting of economic time series data. This data set consists of monthly unemployment rate data for the United States and four individual states, California, New York Oregon, and Texas. This data set ranges from 1976-01-01 to 2026-09-01.

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(tidyquant)

unemp_raw = read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds")

head(unemp_raw)
```

## Wrangling

```{r}
#| label: code
#| include: false 

library(knitr)

unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      symbol == "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
      symbol == "ORUR" ~ "Oregon",
      symbol == "CAUR" ~ "California",
      symbol == "TXUR" ~ "Texas",
      symbol == "NYUR" ~ "New York"
    )
  )

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(
    unemployment_rate = replace(
      unemployment_rate,
      date == as.Date("2025-10-01"),
      unemployment_rate[date == as.Date("2025-09-01")]
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(unemployment_rate_change = unemployment_rate - lag(unemployment_rate)) |>
  ungroup()

unemp_recent <- unemp |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2015-01-01"))

unemp_summary <- unemp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(
    meanrate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate = max(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate = min(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

unemp_recent_summary <- unemp_recent |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(
    meanrateR = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rateR = max(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rateR = min(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

unemp_top_increase_no_covid <- unemp |>
  filter(date < as.Date("2020-01-01") | date > as.Date("2020-12-31")) |>
  slice_max(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5, with_ties = TRUE, na_rm = TRUE)

unemp_top_decreases_no_covid <- unemp |>
  filter(date < as.Date("2020-01-01") | date > as.Date("2020-12-31")) |>
  slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5, with_ties = TRUE, na_rm = TRUE)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
#| label: plots
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment Rate Over Time by Region",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    color = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Create Individual line plots
ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ region, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment Rate Over Time by Region",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Unemployment Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Produce a bar chart
ggplot(unemp_summary, aes(x = fct_reorder(region, meanrate), y = meanrate, fill = region)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Unemployment Rate by Region",
    x = "Region",
    y = "Average Unemployment Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Create your own

top_by_region <- unemp |>
  filter(date < as.Date("2020-01-01") | date > as.Date("2020-12-31")) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, na_rm = TRUE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(label = paste0(format(date, "%b %Y"), "\nRate: ", unemployment_rate, "%"))

ggplot(top_by_region,
       aes(x = reorder(region, unemployment_rate_change),
           y = unemployment_rate_change, fill = region)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), vjust = 1.1, size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Largest Month-Over-Month Decrease in Unemployment by Region",
    subtitle = "Excluding 2020",
    x = "Region",
    y = "Change in unemployment rate (percentage points)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Each bar is the largest month-over-month decrease i the unemployment rate for that region, excluding 2020. The label gives the month and year this occurred as well as the unemployment rate associated with this change. The rate is the unemployment rate after the drop.
